verdict.rationale: Orb's first-party MCP server docs say API keys are scope-controlled per area, with each scope set to none, read or write. The server acts with the connected key's permissions, and out-of-scope tool calls fail with a permissions error, so an agent can get a least-privilege credential. Test-mode keys add isolation from live billing data. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of scope enforcement, a dedicated API-key permissions reference (scoping is described only on the MCP page), and evidence on key expiry or rotation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Each scope covers one area of Orb... and can be set to **none**, **read** or **write**
To try things out without touching live billing data, create the key in **test mode**.
